items.title: Dalio: designing precedes doing, skip it and fail
items.takeaway: Ray Dalio warned that planning time determines effectiveness and that people skip design because they are preoccupied with execution.
items.soWhat: Leaders who skip design burn cycles executing the wrong plan.

items.title: Theo: AI widens the engineer gap to 100×
items.takeaway: Theo shared the prompt suffix “Be thorough in your analysis and bold in your recommendations,” and said AI widened the average-to-best engineer gap to at least 100×.
items.soWhat: Prompt craft and judgment, not more seats, now separate average from elite.

items.title: Nous Arete cuts propaganda answers to under 1%
items.takeaway: Nous Research released Arete-27B, an Apache-2.0 SFT of Qwen3.8-27B that cut propaganda answers on an 803-prompt eval from 22% to 0.9% while lifting fact score 2.32→2.98/5.
items.soWhat: Open weights can be steered on values without tanking core bench scores.

items.title: Anthropic teaches agents to dream between sessions
items.takeaway: Anthropic’s agent-memory post argues agents should note salience in-session and use offline “dreaming” to replay transcripts, build wiki-like maps, and inject a small header into every new session.
items.soWhat: Offline replay is becoming product memory, not a research footnote.

items.title: Anthropic AI R&D pace roughly doubled in a year
items.takeaway: Ajeya Cotra summarized a METR deep-access report: Anthropic capabilities progress roughly doubled Oct 2025–Oct 2026 vs the prior year, mostly from AI automating AI R&D.
items.soWhat: If AI is compounding lab progress, your roadmap clocks are already late.

items.title: Labs share a cyber jailbreak severity scorecard
items.takeaway: The Frontier Model Forum released v1.0 of its Jailbreak Rating Framework for Frontier Cyber Threats, scoring capability gain, scope, ease of deployment, and discovery, with comments open through Dec 21, 2026.
items.soWhat: Shared jailbreak tiers let buyers compare cyber risk across frontier labs.

items.title: Claude Code cloud sessions auto-set your env
items.takeaway: ClaudeDevs said Claude Code cloud sessions on Pro, Max, and Ultra now auto-detect dependencies, network access, and API keys, save the environment, and keep keys hidden from the model.
items.soWhat: Cloud coding agents stop asking you to wire deps and secrets by hand.

items.title: OpenAI ships BioBasicsBench for wet-lab agents
items.takeaway: OpenAI and Ligo introduced BioBasicsBench: 100 tasks from real experiments that measure whether AI agents can interpret raw wet-lab data and handle routine laboratory analyses.
items.soWhat: Wet-lab agents now have a real-experiment scoreboard leaders can track.

items.title: Meta Muse Spaces turn chats into live app hubs
items.takeaway: Meta launched Muse Spaces so users can describe app-like hubs Muse builds and updates from connected apps, plus Active Memory (2.4× less forgetting) and Active Focus (67% better finishing blocked tasks).
items.soWhat: Consumer AI is shipping rearrangeable app surfaces, not just chat replies.

items.title: Muse Spaces: describe a hub, Muse builds the UI
items.takeaway: Users describe a shopping hub, school dashboard, or music tracker; Muse builds it inside the chat app, keeps it updated from connected services, and lets users pin or schedule it in the nav.
items.soWhat: Chat UIs are becoming navigable product surfaces users pin and schedule.

items.title: Libghostty 1.0 makes terminal emulation shared infra
items.takeaway: Mitchell Hashimoto shipped libghostty-vt 1.0 with a stable C ABI now powering JetBrains IDE terminals (~12.5M users), an approved Neovim PR, Vercel Turborepo’s TUI, and agentic tools like herdr and cmux.
items.soWhat: Agent coding tools inherit a correct terminal instead of rewriting one.

image.alt: Mitchell Hashimoto: Libghostty 1.0 makes terminal emulation shared infra

items.title: Libghostty’s stable ABI lets agent TUIs share craft
items.takeaway: Libghostty 1.0 uses opaque handles and enum-keyed getters so new fields do not break ABI, with XCFramework and WASM builds so agentic TUIs inherit a correct emulator.
items.soWhat: Design systems for agent terminals now start from a versioned C ABI.

image.alt: Mitchell Hashimoto: Libghostty’s stable ABI lets agent TUIs share craft

items.title: Signed manifests cut unsafe multi-agent handoffs
items.takeaway: arXiv 2611.07483 finds HMAC-signed requirement manifests with checkable predicates cut unsafe commits under attack versus free-text or structured JSON handoffs.
items.soWhat: Free-text handoffs leak requirements; signed predicates make mergers checkable.

image.alt: arXiv: Signed manifests cut unsafe multi-agent handoffs
